samasa.vigraha: सर्वाणि च तानि भूतानि च, तेषु

samasa.type: karmadhāraya (avadhāraṇa: the first member is the form itself)
samasa.literal: by the form that is hunger
samasa.alt: Also a ṣaṣṭhī tatpuruṣa, क्षुधायाः रूपम्, ‘the form of …’; the karmadhāraya fits the series, where she is that state itself.

morph.note: As in 5.20-22: past participle of सम् + √स्था, the root’s ā becoming i before -ta (स्थित); used as a finite verb, ‘abides’.

mantras.anvaya: या देवी सर्वभूतेषु क्षुधारूपेण संस्थिता, तस्यै नमः, तस्यै नमः, तस्यै नमः नमः (अस्तु)।
mantras.anvaya_en: A relative clause (या देवी … संस्थिता) and its correlative in the dative (तस्यै), governed by the repeated नमः; the same frame as 5.14-16.
mantras.lit: The Goddess who abides in all beings in the form of hunger — to her salutation, to her salutation, to her salutation, salutation.
mantras.tr: To the Goddess who dwells in all beings as Hunger: homage to her, homage to her, homage to her, homage, homage.

comm.t: Hunger, a want rather than a virtue, is named as her form. The series is deliberately inclusive: after intelligence and sleep come hunger, shadow and power, and later thirst (5.35–37) and even error (5.74–76). In chapter 1 hunger already belonged to Mahāmāyā’s work: birds, though tormented by hunger (पीड्यमानानपि क्षुधा), feed their young out of delusion (1.51–52).
A modern reading: to bow to the Goddess as hunger is to refuse to divide life into a sacred part and a merely bodily part. The need that drives every creature is itself where she is met.

sandhi.type: consonant sandhi (ch doubled after a short vowel)
sandhi.note: After a short vowel an initial ch takes the augment t, which becomes c next to ch (स्तोः श्चुना श्चुः, 8.4.40): -u + ch- → -uccha-. After a word-final short vowel the doubling is obligatory (पदान्ताद्वा, 6.1.76, makes it optional only after a long vowel). The Gita Press therefore prints the two words together — the only yā devī stanza where सर्वभूतेषु is joined to the next word.
Visarga before t becomes s; the same in all three नमस्तस्यै.

samasa.vigraha: सर्वाणि च तानि भूतानि च, तेषु

samasa.type: karmadhāraya (avadhāraṇa: the first member is the form itself)
samasa.literal: by the form that is shadow
samasa.alt: Also a ṣaṣṭhī tatpuruṣa, छायायाः रूपम्, ‘the form of …’; the karmadhāraya fits the series, where she is that state itself.

morph.note: As in 5.20-22: past participle of सम् + √स्था, the root’s ā becoming i before -ta (स्थित); used as a finite verb, ‘abides’.

mantras.anvaya: या देवी सर्वभूतेषु छायारूपेण संस्थिता, तस्यै नमः, तस्यै नमः, तस्यै नमः नमः (अस्तु)।
mantras.anvaya_en: A relative clause (या देवी … संस्थिता) and its correlative in the dative (तस्यै), governed by the repeated नमः; the same frame as 5.14-16.
mantras.lit: The Goddess who abides in all beings in the form of shadow (shade) — to her salutation, to her salutation, to her salutation, salutation.
mantras.tr: To the Goddess who dwells in all beings as Shadow: homage to her, homage to her, homage to her, homage, homage.

comm.t: छाया is shadow and shade: the cool shelter from heat and the dark likeness that follows every body; the word can also mean a reflection. The text does not say which sense is meant, and the stanza names the form without explaining it.
A modern reading: the shadow is what a being cannot leave behind. To find the Goddess there is to find her in what accompanies a person unnoticed, as well as in what is seen.

mantras.anvaya: या देवी सर्वभूतेषु शक्तिरूपेण संस्थिता, तस्यै नमः, तस्यै नमः, तस्यै नमः नमः (अस्तु)।

mantras.lit: The Goddess who abides in all beings in the form of power — to her salutation, to her salutation, to her salutation, salutation.
mantras.tr: To the Goddess who dwells in all beings as Power: homage to her, homage to her, homage to her, homage, homage.

comm.t: Śakti is the power or capacity by which anything acts at all. It is also the word the Śākta tradition uses for the Goddess herself, so this stanza names her by her most general name: she is the power in every being.
Brahmā’s hymn in chapter 1 said the same: ‘whatever is the power of all that exists, that is you’ (तस्य सर्वस्य या शक्तिः सा त्वम्, 1.83). The Nārāyaṇī hymn calls her वैष्णवी शक्तिः (11.5).
Lalitā Sahasranāma (Brahmāṇḍa Purāṇa) has the related names 217, महाशक्तिः, and 572, पराशक्तिः. The works are separate.
